The MemAcc module shall allow only one job request per address area.
Once a job request was accepted, the job processing status shall be set to MEMACC_JOB_PENDING .
In case the last memory operation was canceled, the job result shall be set to MEMACC_CANCELED .

The prioritization of memory operations shall use the Mem_Suspend and Mem_Resume service if the memory hardware supports this functionality. If the memory hardware does not support a suspend/resume functionality, the prioritization shall be implemented on a page/page burst, respectively sector/sector burst basis.

The service MemAcc_Init shall initialize the MemAcc module internal states. If MemInvocation (see [ECUC_Mem_00025]) is set to INDIRECT_DYNAMIC or INDIRECT_STATIC , MemAcc_Init shall also initialize all available Mem drivers by calling the Mem driver’s individual initialization functions.

When the MemAcc_Cancel service is called by an upper layer, the MemAcc module shall wait for the completion of a pending Mem job and stop further processing of the current MemAcc job.
In case no MemAcc job is pending, the MemAcc_Cancel service shall just return without any further action, i.e., the result of the last MemAcc job shall not be affected.

An address area shall only be assigned to one upper layer module.
Within a sub-address area, only a uniform sector size is allowed.
Start address and length of address areas shall be aligned to the physical sectors.

The MemAcc module shall support address areas larger than 4GBytes, thus MemAcc_AddressType and MemAcc_LengthType shall be defined as a 64-Bit types in case the address area configuration of one address area exceeds 4GBytes.
If all address areas don’t exceed 4GBytes, MemAcc_AddressType and MemAcc_ LengthType shall be defined as a 32-Bit types.
The MemAcc module implementation shall be hardware independent.

If MemInvocation (see [ECUC_Mem_00025]) is set to INDIRECT_DYNAMIC or INDIRECT_STATIC , MemAcc shall call all Mem main functions within MemAcc_MainFunction . MemAcc_MainFunction shall only call the Mem main function if there is a job request pending for the corresponding Mem driver.

If MemInvocation (see [ECUC_Mem_00025]) is set to DIRECT_STATIC , MemAcc shall call the Mem driver service functions. Otherwise the MemAcc shall call the Mem driver service functions via the Mem driver function pointer table.
If enabled by MemAccUseEraseBurst , MemAcc shall align and split the Mem driver erase requests according to the erase burst size of the Mem driver.

MemAcc shall split the Mem driver read requests according to the maximum read length defined by MemMaxRead if the length of the MemAcc read request is larger than the MemMaxRead value of the respective Mem driver.
If enabled by MemAccUseWriteBurst , MemAcc shall align and split the Mem driver write requests according to the write burst size of the Mem driver.
In case the job processing was completed or no job is currently pending, the job processing status shall be set to MEMACC_JOB_IDLE .
In case the job processing was completed successfully, the job result shall be set to MEMACC_OK .

In case the job processing was completed but the results of the last MemAcc job didn’t meet the expected result, e.g. a blank check operation was applied on a non-blank memory area, the job result shall be set to MEMACC_INCONSISTENT .
In case the last memory operation was completed but the ECC circuit corrected an ECC error, the job result shall be set to MEMACC_ECC_CORRECTED .
In case the last memory operation didn’t complete due to an uncorrectable ECC error, the job result shall be set to MEMACC_ECC_UNCORRECTED .
In case the memory operation was not successfully completed for any other reason, the job result shall be set to MEMACC_FAILED .

The types specified in this chapter shall not be changed or extended for a specific memory abstraction module or hardware platform.
The data type for the memory device index shall be uint8. The lowest value to be used for this device index shall be 0. The allowed range of indices thus shall be 0..MEMIF_ NUMBER_OF_DEVICES-1.

The API specified in this chapter shall be mapped to the API of the underlying memory abstraction modules. For functional behavior refer to the specification of those modules respectively to that of the underlying memory drivers.

The parameter DeviceIndex shall be used for selection of memory abstraction modules (and thus memory devices). If only one memory abstraction module is configured, the parameter DeviceIndex shall be ignored.

If only one memory abstraction module is configured, the Memory Abstraction Interface shall be implemented as a set of macros mapping the Memory Abstraction Interface API to the API of the corresponding memory abstraction module.
If more than one memory abstraction module is configured, the Memory Abstraction Interface shall use efficient mechanisms to map the API calls to the appropriate memory abstraction module.

If more than one memory abstraction module is configured and development error detection is enabled for this module, the functions of the Memory Abstraction Interface API shall check the parameter DeviceIndex for being an existing device or the broadcast identifier within the module’s services.

The functions of the Memory Abstraction Interface API shall report detected errors attributed to an illegal parameter DeviceIndex to the Default Error Tracer (DET) with the error code MEMIF_E_PARAM_DEVICE and the called service shall not be executed.

If a called function of the Memory Abstraction Interface API has detected an error attributed to an illegal parameter DeviceIndex and has a return value, it shall be set as follows: MemIf_GetStatus: MEMIF_UNINIT MemIf_GetJobResult: MEMIF_JOB_FAILED All other functions: E_NOT_OK

For each build scenario (e.g. Boot loader, ECU Application) an own set of memory mapping files has to be provided.

The memory mapping file name shall be {Mip}_MemMap.h for basic software modules and {componentTypeName}_MemMap.h for software components where {Mip} is the Module implementation prefix and {componentTypeName} is the name of the software component type.

Each AUTOSAR basic software module and software component shall wrap declaration and definition of code, variables and constants using the following mechanism: 1. Definition of start symbol for module memory section 2. Inclusion of the memory mapping header file 3. Declaration/definition of code, variables or constants belonging to the specified section 4.…

The memory mapping header files shall provide a mechanism to select different code, variable or constant sections by checking the definition of the module specific Memory Allocation Key Words for starting a section (see [SWS_MemMap_00038]). Code, variables or constants declared after this selection shall be mapped to this section.
The selected section shall be deactivated, if the section stop macro is defined before including of the memory mapping header file.

The memory mapping header files shall check if they have been included with a valid Memory Allocation Keyword and in a valid - not nested - sequence (no START preceded by a START, no STOP without the corresponding START). This shall be done by a preprocessor check.
If a compiler/linker does not require specific commands to implement the functionality of SWS Memory Mapping, the Memory Allocation Keyword defines might be undefined without further effect.
The memory mapping header files shall undefine the module or software component specific Memory Allocation Key Words for starting or stopping a section.
The memory mapping header files shall use if-else structures to reduce the compilation effort.
The selected section shall be activated, if the section start macro is defined before including of the memory mapping header file.
The selection of a section shall not be nested and only influence one of the three different symbol types of code, variables, or constants concurrently.
Each AUTOSAR basic software module and software component shall support, for all C-objects, the configuration of the assignation to one of the memory types (code, variables and constants).

The SWS Memory Mapping is applicable for each AUTOSAR basic software module and software component. Therefore the implementation of memory mapping files shall fulfill the implementation and configuration specific needs of each software module in a specific build scenario.
